messages:
Aisha (Support): Hey team — customer AcmeHealth reports sudden 429s and sustained latency increases starting ~09:15 UTC. They say traffic pattern didn’t change. They see 'quota exceeded' in body for a subset of requests. Can someone triage?
Marco (SRE): Got it. Do we have their API key / customer id? Can you paste an example request/response (headers) and approx qps?
Aisha (Support): Customer ID: cust_08642. Sample response body: `{'error':'rate_limit_exceeded','message':'quota exhausted for tenant'}`. They reported ~120 rps burst for ~2m then drop to ~5 rps. They’re on tier: reserved+burst (monthly commit).
Kai (Customer Success): FYI they recently onboarded a new ingestion job — could be a bug. I’ll loop in their infra contact.
Jules (Platform): Quick checklist: 1) Is this global throttling or per-API-key? 2) Any autoscale events? 3) Any recent policy changes to limits?
Nora (Eng-Platform): I’m pulling throttling logs now. Query I used in Kibana: `service:gateway AND status:429 AND json.payload.customer_id:cust_08642 | stats count() by route, model, api_key`.
Marco (SRE): From infra metrics (last 30m): per-customer token bucket for cust_08642 hit 0 at 09:15:22 UTC and stayed at 0 until 09:17:05. throughput backlog spiked. Looks like burst quota was exhausted.
Aisha (Support): They’re asking how we attribute that — they want to know whether specific route/model caused it so they can fix the producer. Any dashboard panels we can point them to?
Nora (Eng-Platform): Dashboard snippets to share: - Panel: "Throttled requests by customer" (group by customer_id, route, model) - Panel: "Rate limit token usage" (gauge showing current tokens, refill rate) - Panel: "Burst consumption windows" (heatmap by minute).
Nora (Eng-Platform): PromQL examples: `sum by (customer_id,route,model) (increase(api_rate_limited_total[5m]))` and `max by (customer_id) (api_rate_limit_tokens{customer_id!=""})`. Those help attribute.
Jules (Platform): Also include the X headers we expose: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, plus `X-Request-ID`. Ask customer to save full response headers for repro.
Marco (SRE): Short-term mitigation options: 1) grant temporary burst topup for cust_08642 (increase bucket size + refill window) 2) add per-route soft-limit and fallback to lower-cost model on throttle 3) ask client to implement exponential backoff with jitter and idempotency keys.
Aisha (Support): Can we do a quick top-up while we investigate? They’re on an enterprise reserved contract.
billing-bot: Note: cust_08642 has reserved capacity with 10% burst allowance. One-off temporary increase requires approval from finance.
Kai (Customer Success): I’ll get approval for a 30-minute top-up. Meanwhile, can we create an alert that fires when `rate_limit_tokens <= 5%` for any customer? We want to catch exhaustions before customers see 429s.
Nora (Eng-Platform): Alert suggestion: `rate_limit_tokens < 0.05 * rate_limit_capacity` for 3 consecutive 60s windows -> page on production-support, notify customer-success slack channel. Also a warning threshold at 20%.
Marco (SRE): Implementation note: alert needs cardinality controls — group_by customer_id with max 200 tracked customers per rule to avoid pager storms. Also provide aggregated metric: `throttled_requests_total` by customer to surface noisy tenants.
Aisha (Support): For attribution, customer wants list of top 10 routes/models causing throttles with example request_ids. Can we export that?
Nora (Eng-Platform): Yes — run: `es query` -> `service:gateway AND status:429 AND customer_id:cust_08642 | top 10 route, model by count` then include `request_id` examples. I can export CSV and share.
Jules (Platform): Longer term: add per-route token accounting (so heavy-model calls won't starve cheap ones). Roadmap item: model-aware quotas + dynamic fallback.
Marco (SRE): Repro steps to ask customer: 1) capture full request headers+payload, 2) run a controlled burst test (start at 20 rps, ramp 20->200 over 3m), 3) include `X-Request-ID` on each request so we map traces.
Aisha (Support): I’ll forward repro steps and request header checklist. Nora — can you share the Kibana query + CSV by EOD?
Nora (Eng-Platform): On it. I’ll also attach Grafana snapshots for the dashboard panels and put a temporary alert rule in staging for review.
Kai (Customer Success): Thanks team. I’ll update AcmeHealth that we’re applying a 30-min temporary top-up pending billing approval and will send them the dashboards + repro checklist.
Marco (SRE): P.S. small ops tip: when investigating 429 storms, check also `kv-cache` eviction logs — sometimes massive prefix invalidation triggers bursts of recompute that exhaust tokens.
Aisha (Support): Noted. Closing loop when Nora posts the CSV and Jules confirms the top-up change. :thumbsup:
